sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 5.7 'Mavchi bolitil svanim prakriya' (p. 258) lists six Standard-Marathi > Mavchi sound correspondences (su>hu, s>h, -ṇī>-y, li>ni, sā>so, gh>g) and no prosody. sources.citation: Grierson, George A. (ed.) 1907. Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. IX: Indo-Aryan family, Central group, Part III: The Bhil languages, including Khandesi, Banjari or Labhani, Bahrupia, &c. Calcutta: Superintendent of Government Printing. Section 'Mawchi' (Khandesh), pp. 95-97 + specimens 30-32.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. The Mawchi sketch gives pronunciation notes only (broad short a; intervocalic h faintly sounded/dropped with vowel contraction; frequent nasalization; intervocalic r dropped; s > h) then nouns, pronouns, verbs. The volume's only accent remark is the front-matter transcription convention ('When it is necessary to mark an accented syllable, the acute accent is used'), never applied to Mawchi. Cites as authority Varley 1902, A Short Hand-Book of the Mavchi and Pavra Dialects.
